order: Fix the abandoned-worktree sweep in the disposable-checkout module. It recognizes its own leftovers by testing whether a registered worktree's path contains the module's temporary-directory prefix, then removes that worktree and recursively deletes its parent. Two reproductions have landed — CI deleted the OS temp root, because the fixture repository's name carried the prefix, and a delta re-review destroyed a legitimate worktree under a prefix-substring ancestor. Replace the substring test with a structural one, so that a leftover is exactly <tmp>/<prefix>XXXX/checkout and only that immediate parent is ever removed, skip the main worktree as a second belt, and keep the live-checkout exemption. Pin both reproducer shapes as regressions, record the re-review verdict verbatim, and fold its dispositions into the round's ledger. Confine the work to the sweep's identification and removal rule, those regressions and those two roster documents, leaving every module-level constant, every default and all behaviour outside that rule unchanged.
claims: Leftover identification is now structural — a candidate qualifies when its basename is checkout and its parent's basename carries the module's temporary-directory prefix, and that parent alone is ever removed. The main worktree is skipped, and the live-checkout exemption is untouched. Both reproducer shapes are pinned as regressions, and the re-review verdict and its dispositions are recorded. Nothing outside the sweep's identification and removal rule was altered. The verifier suite reports 96 passed, the router suite 135, the registry suite 31.
